one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely dissatisfied with the representation provided by harveys during my interview at Deeside police station.
​Under the Police and Criminal Evidence Act (PACE) 1984, every person in custody has a fundamental right to consult privately with a legal representative of their choice. Instead of upholding this fundamental duty of care and acting in my best interests, this solicitor actively facilitated the police in bypassing my explicit request for my chosen solicitor.
​A solicitor's primary obligation is to protect their client's rights, remain independent from law enforcement, and ensure fair treatment under the law. By enabling the police to deny my statutory right to chosen legal representation, they failed to act in my best interests and undermined the integrity of my defense at a critical moment.
Since the interview was now 2 weeks ago I am also somewhat concerned about the lack of communication from Harveys to myself.
​I cannot recommend Harveys to anyone seeking independent, robust, or client-focused representation in a police station setting.

UPDATED REVIEW- my response to the owner

now that the owner of this business replied with quite a few incorrect statements, I’ll now tell you more detail

I did NOT HAVE TINNITUS BEFORE THIS APPOINTMENT! The appointment was to check for ear wax which there wasn’t any on inspection.. I told Ian on the phone that I was getting a BIT of ringing in my ears and I was worried that my ears might be blocked with wax,  what I meant by a BIT was a second or two of ringing here or there…  and that was actually caused by the olive oil I was using, I also told the woman this on arrival that it was a second or two of ringing.

After the appointment i did end up with permanent full on tinnitus that I suffer with every second of every day and went straight to GP’s and the ENT at peninsula health who confirmed that my ear canals were massively inflamed after the ear irrigation and that there was some scarring to my ear drum, hearing “experts” absolutely did this to me

At the time and from Ian’s own website it states that you’ll only ever be dealt with by him the audiologist, I fully expected him to be present at the appointment and him to examine my ears but on arrival he wasn’t there and I was seen by a woman instead

The fact is hearing “experts” should have known better especially if they’re calling themselves experts , I ask you this owner and readers, should  you irrigate someone’s ears with water if there is no wax in them ? The answer is obviously no, the ENT was shocked when I told him what happened , the look on the gp’s face when I told her what happened was one of disbelief , if I would have went to the nhs or an ent for my issues before I went here , they would have just told me to stop using the olive oil because there is no wax in my ears.

Why was ear irrigation used on me ? If there was no wax in my ears  , this was a huge mistake which hearing expert is at fault for and clearly don’t want to admit and the woman  blasted each ear twice ? For what reason ? No wonder there was severe inflammation in my ear , it was forceful and uncomfortable, it shouldn’t have happened at all and is not something any professional expert would have ever done

this could have been all prevented if I was treated with professional thoughtful care but I was met with a rushed let’s get it done and take your money mindset from a place that didn’t care

Am I upset ? Yes , who wouldn’t be if this happened but I am fair in my review. I think the owners response is quite pathetic and almost trying to worm his way out of it.

. of course I returned demanding a refund after it happened, I signed a piece of paper at the time of refund without reading it , he demanded I sign it if I want a refund.. and for the offers of further care lol I vaguely recall  my dad saying he mentioned it on the phone to him but I decided to go to actual professionals who wouldn’t make it any worse

I write this review to warn others of the dangers of these private businesses who claim to be experts

Be wary of this place, they’re not the experts they claim to be

I Went in for ear wax removal or a check on my ears, I was using olive oil prior to the appointment to soften it , turns out the olive oil was the only thing left in my ears by the time I went to this appointment, NO WAX  at all in my ears ..

it should have ended there!  but the woman thought it was a good idea to go ahead with ear irrigation anyway , to clean out the olive oil left in my ears , she even blasted each ear twice in an attempt to throughly get any olive oil out of them and into the bowl to show me something had been done.. Any good ENT or GP would tell you what was done to me was completely unnecessary, callous and risky..  I ended up with severe inflammation in my ears canals  , some scarring to my ear drum and permanent tinnitus, it’s been just over 5 years since this happened  at this Business and I’ve suffered with constant ringing in my ears everyday.. they took the sound of silence away from me

I’d say the biggest mistake and regret in my life was coming to this place

Extremely disappointing experience — £699 paid and refund not resolved

I paid £699 for this service based on specific information and assurances about the support I would receive. My experience did not match those expectations. I understood that I would have access to a qualified solicitor, yet I ended up dealing with a Case Handler/Case Worker. During a phone call, Martine Miles, Complaint Manager, told me that she could act as my Case Handler and connect me directly with a qualified solicitor.

I also have serious concerns about the Terms & Conditions. I was told they would be sent to me by email, but I did not receive them, and I did not sign or expressly agree to them. Despite this, I was later told that I had agreed to the Terms & Conditions. This was particularly concerning because I had never received the document I was supposedly agreeing to.

The refund process was equally disappointing. I understood that a 30-day refund guarantee applied. When I requested a refund, instead of simply resolving my request, I was repeatedly offered reduced fees to continue with the company. In an email, Martine Miles, Complaint Manager, wrote: “Our offer to continuing the process and reduce your fee by £200.00 still stands.” She then wrote: “Please let me know if you want to close the file down and receive £200.00 refund or continue at the reduced fee mentioned above.” In effect, the options presented to me were to continue with the company at a reduced fee or close my file and receive only £200.

I spent 8 days trying to resolve the matter before having to raise a dispute with my bank. In another email, Martine Miles wrote: “I am sorry if this gave the impression that a full refund had been confirmed.” She also stated: “My offer to refund the unused Clean Break element of your service remains open.” These statements are particularly important because they show in their own written correspondence how the refund was ultimately being handled.

During a phone conversation, I was also asked not to post a review and was given one week for the refund issue to be resolved. I gave them that opportunity, but the matter was not resolved.

I have retained the relevant emails and WhatsApp messages and will share selected excerpts so that potential customers can judge the situation from the correspondence themselves. Based on my experience, I would strongly recommend that anyone considering this company carefully verifies exactly what service they are paying for, who will actually handle their case, what Terms & Conditions they have received and agreed to, and exactly what refund they can realistically expect if they decide not to continue.

Serious concerns regarding patient care, communication, and clinical governance

I wish to formally raise my concerns regarding the standard of care provided by this practice.

From initial contact at reception through to GP consultation, my experience was unsatisfactory. Reception staff were dismissive, lacked professionalism, and failed to demonstrate empathy toward patients presenting with health concerns.

During consultations, clinical decisions were made without appropriate patient involvement or discussion of treatment options. Despite reporting chronic pain and specifically requesting referral for diagnostic imaging, my request was declined. Following a formal complaint, the referral was eventually issued. The subsequent scan confirmed an underlying health condition that warranted earlier investigation.

Practice management appears unable to manage current patient demand. When I requested to speak with the practice manager, the response was unprofessional and unsupportive. Effective complaint handling and patient communication require appropriate management training, particularly within a healthcare setting serving vulnerable and unwell individuals.

Many patients are in employment and rely on timely pain management and accurate diagnosis to access necessary treatment and maintain their livelihood. Delays and dismissive attitudes directly impact patient wellbeing and quality of life.
Other patients can’t get back in to work because of this behaviour towards patients.

In summary, the practice is not delivering patient-centered care. Clinical decisions appear to be made without adequate consideration of the patient’s symptoms, needs, and ongoing impact on daily life. This falls below the standard of care I would expect.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had a very poor experience with Design Cloud and would not recommend them based on how my cancellation was handled.

I signed up for their video editing service and submitted a detailed brief. Shortly afterwards, their team told me that one of the software tools required for the project was not something they used and that I would need to provide the relevant screen recordings myself.

As this was an important part of the work I needed, I decided the service was not the right fit and asked to cancel approximately one hour after subscribing. At that point I had not completed onboarding, no production work had begun, and nothing had been delivered.

Design Cloud refused to refund the payment and said I had committed to a minimum one-month subscription.

What made the experience significantly worse was the response from the company director. Rather than simply dealing with the refund request, he repeatedly told me to watch a Loom video, made comments about me using AI to help write my emails, described my brief as one of the better “ChatGPT briefs” they had received, and then warned me that pursuing a chargeback could potentially cause “future issues” with my bank if they won the dispute.

I found the tone unnecessarily patronising and confrontational, particularly given that I was a brand-new customer attempting to cancel almost immediately.

There was also a noticeable change in how the service was described after I requested cancellation. I was initially told that the screen recordings needed to be supplied by me because they did not use the software. Later, I was told I could simply provide a login and they could record the screens themselves. I was also initially told an onboarding call would be “beneficial”, whereas it was later described as “essential”.

Businesses are entitled to have cancellation and refund policies, but customer service is also about judgment and how those policies are applied. Retaining a full month’s payment from a customer who cancelled roughly an hour after subscribing, before onboarding or any work had taken place, while responding in this manner, left a very bad impression.

I would strongly recommend understanding exactly what is included, what you are expected to supply yourself, and the cancellation terms before paying.

one_star_reviews.text:
Visited for a second time after a pleasant experience around a year ago while visiting my brother, who lives nearby. Unfortunately, this visit was considerably less satisfactory.

We arrived at approximately 8:55pm and ordered food and drinks. After waiting around 30 minutes without an update, the manager—whose name appeared to begin with “Fra…” on the receipt—advised us that some of the food we had ordered was unavailable. We understood that this can happen, but we were not offered clear alternatives, the option to amend the order, or an explanation of whether a refund would be provided. We were left unsure how to proceed and had to seek clarification ourselves.

We eventually received our food and drinks and stayed until around 10pm, when we ordered another round of drinks. Shortly afterwards, the same manager asked two members of our group—my sister and girlfriend—for identification. We were then told to “drink up and leave”. We were not given a clear explanation for this request, nor were we told whether the drinks we had just ordered would be served or refunded.

We appreciate that staff may need to follow licensing requirements or manage closing procedures, particularly during a busy Bank Holiday weekend. We would have been happy to comply if these requirements had been explained clearly and at the appropriate time. However, the communication on this occasion was inconsistent: we were able to place a substantial food and drink order after 9pm, but were then asked to leave shortly after ordering further drinks. Our group was not being excessively loud or disruptive, so the lack of explanation made the decision feel abrupt and poorly handled.

The main issue was not that certain items were unavailable or that we were asked to leave, but that the relevant information was not communicated clearly. We would have expected staff to explain the available alternatives, confirm any refund arrangements, and provide a clear reason and timescale when asking us to finish our drinks and leave.

This was disappointing, particularly given how enjoyable our previous visit had been, and it has left us with a significantly less positive impression of the venue.

AVOID THIS COMPANY - they took my money, failed to deliver my order and then effectively disappeared.

I placed order 1266600 with Bathrooms & Showers Direct on 18 July. Their confirmation stated that the order would be dispatched within 10 working days.

It is now 20 August. More than a month later, I have NO GOODS, NO DISPATCH CONFIRMATION and not even an ETA.

But the delay itself is not the worst part. The customer service has been absolutely appalling.

On 20 July, they specifically promised to update me within 3 working days. That update never came.

I chased them repeatedly by email. No meaningful response.

I raised a FORMAL COMPLAINT. No response.

I sent a FINAL NOTICE. They replied that they will check with supplier and promised to provide update and call me. They never called me or wrote back after checking with supplier.

I repeatedly tried to contact them by telephone. I could not get through.

At this point, I genuinely cannot understand how a company can take payment for an order, miss its own stated dispatch timeframe by weeks, provide no ETA and then simply stop communicating with the customer.

I have now cancelled the order and contacted my credit card provider to recover my money.

I very rarely leave reviews like this, but this experience deserves one. A delay can happen to any retailer. What is completely unacceptable is leaving a paying customer chasing for weeks while providing neither the goods, a delivery date nor basic communication.

Based on my experience, I would strongly recommend buying elsewhere.

One of the worst online shopping experiences I have had.

I have visited many Kokoro outlets over the years, but unfortunately, the Watford branch has consistently stood out for the wrong reasons. On this occasion, both the quality of the food and the attitude of the staff were extremely disappointing.

We visited at approximately 7:50 pm. The food we were served was significantly overcooked and had very little taste. The chicken in particular was extremely dry, tough and chewy—to the point that my son could not even chew it properly.

We barely ate the meals before returning them. I have attached a photograph of the returned food, which clearly shows that only approximately two bites had been taken from each dish.
What made the experience considerably worse was the behaviour of one female member of staff. When I tried to explain the problem, I found her manner extremely rude, dismissive and disrespectful. She simply told me that the manager was not there, turned her face away from me and began looking at and attending to someone else while I was still trying to speak to her. There was no apology, no attempt to understand the complaint and no effort to resolve the situation.

I also want to raise something more serious. I was very uncomfortable with the difference between the way this member of staff treated me and the way she interacted with other customers. From her behaviour, I was left with the impression that she did not want to attend to me because I was not of a certain race, while appearing noticeably friendlier and more attentive towards others. I cannot know her intentions, but this was genuinely how the interaction made me feel, and I believe such a concern should be taken seriously and investigated rather than dismissed.

I am particularly disappointed because I have eaten at many Kokoro branches and know that this experience is not representative of the standard I have experienced elsewhere. However, my experiences at the Watford branch have been by far the worst in terms of both food and customer service.

I would like Kokoro to investigate this incident, including the conduct of the staff member concerned and the quality of food being served towards the end of the day. We returned virtually untouched because of their quality.

I have been left utterly distressed by Coop funeral care, specifically the Warrington branch but also the company in general following further issues with the complaints team.

A ring which was logged on the receipt I got when she went to the funeral home went missing. When the home noticed, rather than calling me they just deleted it from the system and the paper copy mysteriously vanished. Luckily I had kept mine. It came to light when I asked the day before the funeral if I would get the rings on the day of the funeral or need to collect them the following week. They told me someone would call me the day after the funeral to discuss. No-one did...

Lorraine the manager in Warrington was investigating. She frequently didn't call me back at the time and date the promised so I had to chase for updates. They investigated and the outcome was 'inconclusive'. I asked her at the beginning if I need to report to the police and Lorraine told me she would report to the police once she had completed the investigation. Once she delivered her outcome, she told me they wouldn'0t do this as no evidence of theft. She delayed me from reporting this and now the police cannot help as too much time has elapsed.

I raised a formal complaint, Lorraine told me they would call me within a few days. I had no call. I called the  complaints team who said they never had this message to call me and would issue an resolution letter shortly. I said how, you havent even spoken to me about my complaint. At this point its not just the missing ring, its the misinformation, failure to maintain contact and horrific service.

one_star_reviews.text:
AVOID THIS PREP CENTRE!

We started working with Prep365 early this year. In our initial call, Lewis told us that they would be able to handle our requirements without issue. Two weeks into the service, they told us that they would not be able to assist us further. This was not necessarily a problem, but the lack of professionalism that followed was.

We were assured that all remaining units we had at their warehouse would be shipped out in a timely manner. This was not the case.

Under their care, multiple units went missing/allegedly not been delivered. We continually chased them for months about our missing units, to which we would always receive the same response: that the warehouse team were looking into it. Eventually, roughly 3 months later, Prep365 declared these SKUs lost. They stated that units had never arrived, however this was impossible, as multiple deliveries required that a passcode must be presented to the delivery driver. Due to the delay on their side, any loss mitigation we could have implemented was no longer possible.

Eventually, they reimbursed us roughly half of the amount which was lost under their supervision. This led to our company incurring large losses at face value, with even larger losses incurred due to the waste of time and resources tied up in dealing with Prep365.

To summarise: communication throughout our experience was abhorrent, they lacked serious professionalism when addressing the problems we had experienced through using their service, and we incurred significant losses through choosing to use Prep365 as our initial prep centre.

The current prep centre we are with is brilliant, and we wish we found them first.

It was my misfortune to come across this company and deciding to use them for their services...

From April 2026, we used Prep 365 as our preparation centre. During this time, we had issues with 6 different SKUs that were delivered to their warehouse, but they never shipped them to Amazon or accounted for them.

Because of our repeated pristence they eventually claimed liability in writing for four of those six SKUs after months of chasing.

The biggest problem was how long it took to get a clear answer. For one consignment, we were told for about two months that the missing units were in the warehouse and being located during a ‘reorganisation’. We kept asking for a definite answer if the stock hadn’t arrived. It wasn’t until weeks later that we were told the units ‘must have been lost in transit’.

On another SKU, we were given three different explanations at different times: that the parcel was delivered and left outside working hours, that they hadn’t taken delivery at all and that fewer units had arrived than were sent. The deliveries required an OTP, meaning a person at the address had to hand the driver a code in person.

We also had units shipped to Amazon incorrectly prepared, which were returned as customer returns on work we had paid a kitting fee for.

Any preparation centre will occasionally lose a box—that is just part of the job. What matters is what happens after that.. Just a heads-up: if you are using Prep365 or are considering them as your fulfilment partner, it might be worth being cautious. They offer discounts on shipping fees for leaving a five-star review, and I have noticed them removing negative reviews from this platform.

A hugely disappointing experience and, in our opinion, a complete waste of time, money and energy.

We had been dealing with bed bugs for a couple of months. We’d tried to deal with the problem ourselves but were struggling, so we reached out to JG Pest Control because we genuinely needed professional help.

Before booking, Bradley told us that treating a 3-bedroom house should take around 40–60 minutes to ensure it was suitably sprayed. Nico was in and out in approximately 12 minutes.

We weren’t expecting an instant result and understood that the treatment would take time to work. However, afterwards we discovered an entire colony of live bed bugs in our headboard.

What makes this particularly frustrating is that the headboard had been completely untouched by the treatment, despite Nico telling us, “I have treated all areas.” Simply saying all areas have been treated doesn’t make it so, and finding an entire live colony in an area that hadn’t been touched has left us seriously questioning how thorough the treatment actually was.

We had already contacted the company asking them to return and carry out a more thorough treatment, but Danielle told us they couldn’t legally return for two weeks. After discovering the colony, we decided it was pointless contacting them again. We’d already lost confidence in the treatment and didn’t feel there was any point waiting another two weeks, so we’ve decided to tackle the problem ourselves.

£546 for around 12 minutes of treatment, and we’re now back to doing the job ourselves. We contacted JG Pest Control because we were stuck and needed professional help, and unfortunately we feel we’ve been left exactly where we started — only considerably out of pocket.

I used Lancashire Double Glazing to have a window fitted in a converted garage. They installed this fine but the internal plaster finish was fairly poor. The repairs have now been booked in 5 times, the first 3 were cancelled for various reasons, each time I had to call them to find out no one was coming. At this point I registered a complaint which I waited a week with no appointment until the fourth appointment rolled round this time the person sent out was not a plasterer and incapable of doing the job and could only apologise. I called to add to my complaint I was advised no installation managers were available to discuss as one was on leave and one was out on site. After I expressed dissatisfaction with waiting until next week for a callback a manager miraculously became available. John was the name given his lack of empathy was staggering to me he advised that it had been booked in and that all he could do. I mentioned all the issues including this being my office where I work from home everyday meaning I'd repeatedly cleared it out only for no one to turn up. I asked about compensation for the inconvenience which he replied with "We don't do that"
I've used LDG a few years ago and they were genuinely great but something has clearly changed over the last few years as this experience has been appalling so far.

I was again advised they "don't offer financial compensation or refunds for inconvenience of this nature" but in my case they would offer a £75 amazon gift card as a small gesture (Which I have received) as they acknowledged the service should have been better. I had an appointment at 11.10am on Friday 21st August.

I sent the text below as an email complaint later that day. I have had no response at all.

The appointment was not the most pleasant experience I have ever had. There were two sonographers present, I cannot tell you their names as I'm not sure I was even told them, but both were quite difficult to understand, so I may have missed the names.

Upon entering the room, I was told to put my belongings on a chair and lie on the bed. I was initially confused as I thought I was just having an internal scan, and so I started to remove my trousers and pants. It was only at this point that I was told that I would first be having an external scan.

Given that the the whole procedure is quite intimate, I would have expected to have had some explanation before being asked to lie on the bed. I had a pelvic exam with my practice nurse last Tuesday, and she took time explain everything and make sure I fully understood before anything else happened.

The 'bedside manner' of the sonographer actually doing the scan was, at best, perfunctory. It would have helped me to feel at ease, and relaxed to have had a better explanation, and perhaps some ongoing conversation, as there has been in previous similar experiences.

I left the appointment feeling like I had simply been 'processed'. On the basis that healthcare is a 'caring' profession. I did not feel particuarly cared for.

Bearing in mind that my appointment was at 11.10am, I was quite shocked at 2.32pm to receive a text with a document to download, which turned out to be a blank consent form! It was only at this point that I realised that I had not been presented with that form at the appointment. At no point was consent obtained, other than me being present for the appointment, and at no point was a chaperone offered. I am at a loss to know what I am supposed to do with the blank consent form, after the fact.

I feel that your procedures need some serious attention, and perhaps the sonographers in question need some further training to improve their bedside manner.

one_star_reviews.text:
AVOID! I instructed Halsalls a month ago for the purchase of my new property. I am a first time buyer who was assured Halsalls could represent me in my purchase. After weeks of me checking in, I have been assured in multiple occasions that things were underway and that they have been waiting on the sellers solicitors to progress the sale. LIES. They first told me they hadn’t received the memo of sale. I discovered from my estate agent that not only had they received it but that it had been opened and read by Carl Horstman who is in charge of conveyancing. After informing them of this they cheerfully revealed that it had in fact been received and read by Carl (who knows how long this would have gone unnoticed if not for me reminding them). Weeks have passed where I have been assured that things are progressing and waiting on outside information. However, yesterday I received an email from Carl, informing me that not only had nothing been done, but that he has been on holiday and knew nothing about my case. Carl then went on to inform me that he was “too busy” to take my case and that I would need to find another solicitor, despite the firm telling me that things were moving forward. He then claimed that although frustrating this has not cost me any time. YET MORE LIES. It has cost me at least a month, and I now have to find a new solicitor and go through the entire process again, as well as having to inform seller, mortgage broker, and estate agents that everything will have to be restarted with a new solicitor.

I don’t know what kind of professional firm behaves this way, takes money from you, claims the process is underway, only to reveal that they’re not going to do the job. All the while I have been told that Carl is on the case.. he has actually been on holiday, and nothing has been done. Not only have they lied and gone back on the instruction, they did not even call to tell me any of this. I received an email which amounted to nothing more than “sorry we’re not doing it”. If I treated my emails the same as they do, I may not have found this out for weeks, because they did not even bother to call me, I assume due to cowardice. I advise anyone who wants a smooth purchase or sale to avoid Halsalls like the plague. They will waste your time, and based on my experience, lie throughout. Sadly I cannot enter 0 Stars.

one_star_reviews.text:
WARNING & CAUTION TO POTENTIAL SELLERS:

I strongly advise potential sellers to think twice before hiring Whitegates. What started as a simple request to fix a poorly taken property photograph has escalated into a formal dispute currently under review by The Property Ombudsman.

Here are the key details of the substandard service and negligence we experienced:

1. Substandard Marketing, Rushed Work & Early Disregard:

* Poor Photography Angles & Misleading Advice: The entire photography visit lasted barely 10 minutes. Before taking the shots, the photographer explicitly told us to leave everything as it was, assuring us that AI would remove any items or clutter. The resulting main photo showed our house occupying only about 25% of the frame, with our wheelie bins right in the center foreground, alongside a large portion of an unkempt neighbouring property. This left prospective buyers confused about which property was actually being advertised (see attached photos showing the initial bad angle with bins, and the second distant shot).
* Early Ignored Requests: We noticed the poor quality immediately after the listing went live. I asked for the photo be replaced the following morning, but our concerns were ignored. The photo demonstrated a total lack of professionalism and directly harmed our property's market appeal.
* Belated Action After Formal Escalation: A second photo was taken later from even further away without informing us. Astonishingly, three months into the contract - and only after we escalated the matter to The Property Ombudsman - the manager quietly updated the listing and used AI to edit out the bins as originally requested and promised. Doing the bare minimum months late sums up their approach.

2. Dismissive Communication, Arrogance & Management Negligence:

* Condescending In-Office Behaviour: When we visited the branch to discuss these issues, we were met with a dismissive and condescending attitude, as if we were begging for a favour rather than being paying clients. We faced an aggressive defence of the poorly taken photo, even though the issue could have easily been resolved in minutes with a simple apology and a new picture.
* Managerial Inaction & Delay: We approached the branch director hoping for a reasonable resolution, but our complaint was ignored for nearly a week. Only after sending a follow-up email requesting termination of the contract did we get a disappointing response which was simply that she was waiting for the branch manager who took the photo to return the following week to respond to us.
* Unfounded Blame by Branch Manager: Subsequently, Branch Manager James rejected our formal complaint and unfairly attempted to shift the blame onto us, claiming the house was "cluttered." This is untrue; the house was clean and well-kept. We had been explicitly instructed to leave the items in the photos where they were, with assurances that they would be edited out digitally.

3. Unfair Financial Demands & Refusal to Terminate (Dispute Over £350 Fee):

* Unjustified Exit Fees: Whitegates heavily markets its services under a "No Sale, No Fee" promise. However, James refused our request to end the agreement and unreasonably insisted that even after fulfilling the 18 week minimum contract term (on Oct 5), and upon providing proper written notice, we would still be forced to pay a £350 withdrawal fee just to walk away.
* Violation of Consumer Expectations: Demanding a termination fee upon the natural expiration of a fixed-term contract is a direct breach of basic consumer expectations and unfair practice.

Conclusion: An extremely poor experience defined by arrogance, negligence, and a complete lack of professionalism. I strongly advise sellers to avoid Whitegates altogether.

one_star_reviews.text:
Think very carefully before renting through Charters

My experience with this company has been extremely disappointing from start to finish.

The property was originally managed by Beales before being transferred to Charters. Unfortunately, the change of agent did nothing to improve the situation. Quite the opposite — whenever something went wrong, communication was poor and repairs seemed to take an unacceptable amount of time.

The worst example was a water leak through the bathroom ceiling which went on for over six weeks. Plumbers were sent out and, incredibly, we were essentially left with the response that there was “a leak there somewhere.” Despite repeated visits, the problem wasn't properly resolved. Eventually, the ceiling collapsed. Having to live with water coming through the ceiling for that length of time is completely unacceptable.

The communal areas were no better. The bin sheds were allowed to become absolutely disgusting, including overflowing over Christmas, and it took weeks to sort out. Residents moving out were also leaving unwanted furniture in the sheds, yet there appeared to be little or no action taken. Other tenants were moving out or complaining about the issues

Then came the end of the tenancy.

There was very little communication about the inspection, leaving us unclear about when it would actually take place. Following the inspection, issues were raised and money was subsequently taken by the landlord.

I understand that Charters are the managing agent and don't personally own the properties they manage. However, that doesn't excuse poor communication, delays in dealing with serious maintenance issues or a lack of proper management of communal areas.

For me, the whole experience was incredibly frustrating and left a very poor impression of the company.

If you're considering renting a property through Charters, I would strongly recommend doing your homework first and thinking very carefully before committing. My experience has been one of delays, poor communication and problems that seemed to take far too long to resolve.

Definitely not an experience I would want to repeat, and not a company I would recommend based on my experience.

I complained about the quality of the repairs two more times, and each time the situation was the same. one_star_reviews.text:
Unfortunately, my experience at this rehabilitation and detox centre was very disappointing. There were a number of serious issues that, in my opinion, need to be addressed.
Communication between the office staff and medical team was poor, and after 8:00pm there were no office staff available. At times, there was only one nurse available and no doctor on site, which left me feeling that there was insufficient medical support when it was needed.
I also experienced issues with medication times and the duration of medication being prescribed. Although concerns were raised with office staff, it often felt as though they listened but little or nothing was done to resolve the problems.
The group meetings were also disappointing and did not provide the level of support I expected from a rehabilitation centre. There were very few meaningful activities, and I felt that patients were often expected to provide emotional support to other patients rather than receiving appropriate professional support themselves. There were also very limited opportunities for one-to-one meetings with office staff.
Overall, the environment felt more like a prison than a rehabilitation or detoxification centre. Patients were often treated more like children than adults receiving treatment, which I found frustrating and upsetting.
There was also a lack of basic evening snacks, which seems like a small issue but made a difference, particularly when patients are going through detox and recovery.
The facilities and level of care provided did not, in my opinion, match the impression given by the centre's website. I was particularly concerned about patients being admitted with mental health needs when it appeared that staff did not always have a sufficient understanding of, or ability to support, those individual needs.
Sadly, I would not recommend this centre to anyone who is genuinely looking for help with addiction or detoxification. I came away feeling that financial considerations appeared to take priority over the individual needs and wellbeing of patients.
People seeking rehabilitation are often at an extremely vulnerable point in their lives. They deserve compassionate care, proper communication, appropriate medical support and individualised treatment. Unfortunately, that was not my experience here.

The very next day, I received a call from one of their team members, Atif, who told me that he had reviewed my case and that he could book me an appointment for a consultation. Based on what I had been told, I travelled all the way from Liverpool to Manchester to attend their office.
Here is the most disgusting part: they took my consultation fee first, and immediately after I paid, they told me that they could not take my case and that I would have to find a private solicitor instead.

Seriously? Why did you ask me to send all my documents, tell me that a solicitor was available, review my case, book me an appointment, make me travel from Liverpool to Manchester, and then take my money before telling me that you could not represent me?
This is an absolutely unprofessional, misleading and disgraceful way to treat someone who is already dealing with an asylum case and looking for legal aid. If you knew from the beginning that you could not take my case, you should have told me BEFORE wasting my time, making me travel, and charging me a consultation fee.
I am extremely disappointed and angry with the way I was treated. Think twice before approaching this firm. In my experience, their communication was completely unacceptable and the whole process felt like an absolute waste of my time and money.
I would strongly advise people to ask very clearly whether their case is actually eligible and whether the firm can take it under legal aid BEFORE travelling to their office or paying any fees.
Absolutely disgraceful experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
Absolutely appalling service — avoid this company.

I have experienced an astonishing level of incompetence from this company. I had an annual servicing and CP12 plan for my rental property and, despite paying for a service that should be straightforward to arrange, I had to make around 10 phone calls simply to get the first appointment booked.

When it was eventually booked, the appointment was cancelled with less than 24 hours’ notice due to illness. Fair enough — these things happen, and I was perfectly understanding. However, I then had to chase them yet again to arrange another appointment, requiring a further two phone calls before it was finally booked for the following day. I even received a text confirmation the day before.

So imagine my surprise when I called the following day, after the service was supposed to have taken place, only to be told that the appointment had been cancelled again.

This time, however, nobody had bothered to tell me.

Their explanation was that a message had supposedly been left for the estate agent. The estate agent says no such message was ever received. Regardless of who is telling the truth, the fact remains that I was given no notification whatsoever that the appointment had been cancelled.

What was particularly disappointing was the complete lack of accountability. There was no meaningful apology, no attempt to rectify the inconvenience they had caused, and no sense that they understood that I had already spent a ridiculous amount of time chasing them. Instead, I was simply offered another appointment for the following week — as though wasting their customer's time repeatedly is perfectly acceptable.

After almost two years of this sort of service, I finally decided enough was enough and cancelled my servicing plan. I explicitly instructed the operator to cancel it. They assured me they would do so, but given the company's track record, I have absolutely no confidence that even this relatively simple instruction will be carried out correctly. I have therefore had to cancel the direct debit myself to make sure I am not charged again.

I also have serious doubts that I will receive a refund for the money I have already paid, but I will be pursuing this through a formal complaint.

A servicing plan is supposed to provide peace of mind and reliable service. Instead, this company has provided repeated cancellations, endless phone calls, poor communication and an astonishing lack of accountability.

I would not recommend this company. If this experience is representative of their normal standard of service, I would strongly advise looking elsewhere.

one_star_reviews.text:
Unfortunately, a very disappointing experience with HiQ Tyres – I do not recommend them.
I collected my car from my mechanic on Thursday, 23 July. The front and rear shock absorbers had been replaced, and the wheels had been refurbished and repainted. New tyres were also fitted to the rear, while the previous rear tyres were moved to the front because they were still in good condition and the car is front-wheel drive.
After the repairs, I drove the car until Monday, 27 July, including to work and the shops. I noticed some minor vibrations and that the car was louder than before. I contacted my mechanic, who recommended having the wheel alignment checked and adjusted.
On Monday, 27 July, I went to HiQ Tyres to have the wheel alignment done. After the service I was not given a printout showing the alignment readings before and after the adjustment. I was told this was their policy and they do not provide such printouts. If I had known beforehand, I would have taken a photo of the readings.
After the wheel alignment, from Tuesday to Thursday, the car was practically undriveable at all. It was extremely noisy, and at higher speeds the steering became unstable and it was difficult to keep the car straight.
On Thursday after work, I went back to my mechanic to check whether the problem could have been caused by the previous repairs. After checking the car again, he found that one of the wheels was not correctly aligned, with an incorrect angle causing it to point inwards. He also noticed that the outer edges of two front tyres had started to wear excessively and become noticeably scrubbed, which had not been the case before.
On 3 August, I returned to HiQ Tyres to make a complaint because I believed the wheel alignment had not been carried out correctly. Unfortunately, instead of calmly investigating the issue, I was accused of trying to get them to pay for new tyres and was told that the wheel alignment had been done correctly.
After a heated exchange, they put the car back on the alignment machine. The readings shown on the monitor clearly raised concerns about the alignment, with some of the measurements outside the correct range. Despite this, the employee claimed that the problem was caused by the steering wheel being crooked. He then blamed the issue on allegedly bent wheels and worn steering rods. I was also told that I was trying to get new tyres from them.
That same day, I booked an appointment with another garage. Unfortunately, I had to wait another week.
After the car was inspected at the second garage, I asked whether the wheels and steering rods were in good condition. I was told that the wheels and steering rods were fine. I also asked about the excessive wear on the outer edges of the tyres. After the wheel alignment was correctly adjusted, the readings were within the correct range, as shown on the attached printout – before the adjustment, some measurements were outside the acceptable range, while after the adjustment they were all within the green area.
After driving the car for a week, I can confidently say that the problem has disappeared. The car now drives properly, there are no more vibrations, and the steering wheel no longer shakes while driving.
What disappointed me most about this whole situation was not only the fact that the service appears to have been carried out incorrectly, but also the way my complaint was handled. Instead of properly investigating the issue, I was accused of trying to get free tyres, while responsibility for the problem was shifted onto other parts of the car. In the end, another garage inspected the vehicle and, after correctly adjusting the wheel alignment, the car started driving properly again.
My experience with HiQ was therefore very disappointing, and I cannot recommend this garage. Based on my experience, I recommend checking the work that has been carried out and asking for a printout of the wheel alignment measurements before and after the adjustment. In my case, not having this documentation made it much more difficult to establish what had actually happened.

We came here after having a bad experience elsewhere, only for our experience here to be even worse.

When we handed the car over for four new tyres, we specifically stressed how concerned we were about the alloys being damaged. We were reassured that there was absolutely nothing to worry about, that they would take care when fitting the tyres, and that the previous company we had used had a bad reputation.

When the car was returned to us, it had been left parked on the main road rather than within the courtyard, which was disappointing in itself. We checked the car over and immediately noticed significant damage to the alloys.

When we raised this with them, they tried to claim that the damage was already there. This was simply not true. We know the condition the alloys were in when we handed the car over, and we had specifically raised our concerns about protecting them beforehand.

What is most disappointing is their complete lack of accountability and unwillingness to take responsibility for the damage.

Based on our experience, we would strongly recommend avoiding this company if you care about your vehicle and want it returned in the condition you left it in.

EDITED to respond: the fact that your response immediately attempts to blame another company speaks volumes.

For clarity, the issues we referred to in our review involved a completely different car - a Mercedes AMG that we owned in 2023 and subsequently sold that same year. They have absolutely nothing to do with the car you had in your possession.

When we dropped this car off with you, we specifically explained our precious experience and why we were particularly concerned about the possibility of something similar happening again. We raised this with you precisely because we wanted the condition of the car, and in particular, the wheels, to be treated with care. At the time the car was handed over, the alloys were in excellent, undamaged condition.

Our concerns were therefore not based on some historic issue with the car, nor are we attempting to attribute pre-existing damage to your company. We are raising an issue that occured while it was in your care.

Rather than addressing the concerns we have raised, your response appears to focus on discrediting our account and shifting responsibility. That does not change the condition the car was in when it was handed over to you, or the condition in which it was returned.

We have no reason to make any of this up and we stand by what we have said in our review. We left the car with you expecting it to be returned in the same condition in which it was left, and unfortunately that was not our experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would absolutely not recommend Mann Island Finance or Citroën Vertu Worcester based on my experience.

I have had a terrible experience dealing with both companies. When problems arose with the vehicle, I expected the finance company to properly consider my concerns and act fairly as the consumer. Instead, I have felt as though they have simply sided with their financial/dealer partner and left me, the customer, to deal with the consequences.

It has felt like hitting a brick wall at every stage. Rather than helping to resolve the situation, I have been left feeling completely unsupported and pushed from one party to another.

My experience has left me with the impression that the priority is collecting the finance payments rather than properly addressing the customer’s concerns when something goes wrong.

I have spent a considerable amount of time trying to get this situation resolved and have found the whole process incredibly frustrating and disappointing. I certainly would not choose either company again based on how I have been treated.

If you are considering purchasing a vehicle from Citroën Vertu Worcester or financing through Mann Finance, I would strongly recommend doing your research and considering how complaints and disputes are handled before committing yourself.

A thoroughly disappointing experience from start to finish.

I purchased two packs of medicine and was charged £30 in total. I was specifically told that the Canesten Combi, which contains one pessary/vaginal tablet and an external cream, cost £20.

However, I have since checked the price of the same product at other major pharmacies. For example, superdrug currently lists Canesten Thrush Combi 500mg Pessary & 2% External Cream at £9.99.

When I questioned the price and requested a refund, my request was refused. I then accepted this and simply asked for a receipt.

What happened next was extremely concerning. The receipt I was given did not contain the names of the medicines I had purchased at all. Even more surprisingly, although I had purchased only two medicines, the receipt showed three separate items, each priced at £9.90

I would also like to point out that only two months ago, I purchased the same Canesten Combi from the same pharmacy and paid £10 for it. On this occasion, I was charged £20 for exactly the same medicine.

Avoid!!! I went to the Wigan branch to exchange just €300. I brought my driving licence, which shows both my name and address.

I was then told that this wasn’t sufficient and that I needed to provide two forms of ID showing my name and address, as well as proof of income. I was also asked about taking pictures of my ID and personal information.

For a €300 currency exchange, I found this excessive. What makes it even more worse is that I have previously used Eurochange at the Trafford Centre and was able to make a currency exchange without being subjected to anything like this for a higher amount.

I completely understand that businesses have legal obligations around identity checks and anti-money-laundering procedures. However, the requirements should be clearly explained and applied consistently. Being asked for income and source-of-funds documentation for such a small everyday travel-money transaction is ridiculous.

I have never experienced such a complete lack of compassion, empathy and basic human understanding from a funeral service.
At one of the most heartbreaking times imaginable, when a family is grieving and simply wants the opportunity to say a final goodbye to their loved one, we were made to feel as though our feelings meant absolutely nothing.
The restrictions placed on our family by Racheal and Stephen were devastating. We understand that there may be procedures that have to be followed, but there is a huge difference between following procedures and treating grieving family members with dignity and compassion. Unfortunately, that distinction seemed to be completely lost here.
A funeral service is supposed to help families through one of the most painful experiences of their lives. Instead, our experience added even more hurt, anger and distress to an already unbearable situation.
The fact that our family was left feeling that we could not even have the final goodbye we wanted is something that will stay with us for a very long time. You only get one opportunity to say goodbye. You cannot give that moment back once it has been taken away.
I sincerely hope Rachael and Stephen never have to experience the same heartbreak themselves, because perhaps then they would understand just how cruel and insensitive this experience has felt.
Our loved one deserved dignity, respect and a proper farewell. Our family deserved compassion.
Sadly, this funeral service failed us when we needed understanding the most.
I would not recommend this service to anyone based on our experience. Think very carefully before entrusting such an important and emotional time to them.

If this is the level of communication over a relatively small job, I personally wouldn’t feel comfortable trusting the company with a larger or more expensive one. We’ll now be getting quotes elsewhere.

A real shame, as I always try to support local businesses, but basic communication and keeping promises to customers shouldn’t be too much to expect.

Private patients should be aware that urgent support is provided through the Royal Marsden NHS hotline and urgent care service rather than a dedicated private service. The urgent care service operates Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm. Despite paying private fees, there is no dedicated private urgent support, and patients are expected to rely on NHS urgent services.

We felt also surprised to receive an additional charge for a telephone consultation that we had not requested. The call lasted only a few minutes, yet an additional charge was applied despite there being no change in the direction of the treatment plan, no new medication being prescribed, and no additional intervention being recommended.

I chose private care because I expected continuity, accessibility and reassurance throughout my treatment. Unfortunately, my experience with urgent support and aftercare fell well short of those expectations.

I’ll be writing to Vitality requesting a refund however I have no doubt they’ll claim that their premiums were used providing free coffees and discounts.  Guess what you absolute con artists -  I didn’t pay £5k for free coffee once a month, I paid it to cover health issues for myself and employees when it is needed most and I cannot think of anything worse than having Vitality onboard in your time of need. Just recently I contracted shingles for the 4th time over several years. Last one 2yrs ago, then after having antivirals prescribed by the local pharmacy. I contracted it again, they woukd not prescribe back to back antivirals without a  Dr's authorisation. High Pastures, my surgery over 52 years, couldn't help  & referred me to call 111. After a couple of conversations, on 111 a duty consultant called me & authorised the antivirals. He told me to make an appointment with my GP for further health checks as 5 shingles attacks is quite rare, & needed investigating. Duly I did,make an appointment, waited for 2 weeks & went on Friday 4th. After a discussion as to whether it was actually shingles, although it had been previously diagnosed, several times & believe me I recognise it at once. She confirmed there was a letter from the consultant, & she then proceeded to say that she would refer me back to him & await their reply. I was in shock & felt so exasperated by the 3 ring circus approach. The standards here have fallen badly. I no longer  know any of the doctors & I lack confidence on decisions making. It is worrying to think that my immunity may be compromised & needs test. I'm being passed back & forth. This surgery has served it's patients well over the years,  for my family, but standards have slipped massively recently it is worrying & so very disappointing.
Regards
V Carroll.

We ordered clothing for a student attending Sparsholt College, but some of the items were unsuitable. In particular, even the smallest size of overalls was far too large and simply not suitable for a small framed female student.

Creative Images accepted the returned items and agreed to refund us, but we were told that we would only receive our money back once the clothing had been “re-allocated” to future customer orders. There was therefore no certainty as to when, or even if, we would receive our refunds.

After a very long and drawn out process involving numerous emails and repeated chasing, we have finally received both refunds. Coincidentally, following our latest chase, we were advised that other orders had come in and the items could now be re-allocated.

While we are pleased the refunds have finally been received, it should never have required this amount of time and persistence to get our money back.

Based on our experience, we cannot recommend Creative Images. Anyone ordering embroidered college clothing should be fully aware of the returns/re-allocation arrangements before purchasing.

one_star_reviews.text:
Really upsetting and frankly bizarre experience at the door tonight.

My best friend and I are both bisexual women and both very femme-presenting. We arrived without tickets and were asked if we had tickets. When we said no, we were told they were “really busy” and directed to Divine down the road instead by a femme presenting person on the door.

As we started walking away, we immediately heard the same door person ask two women behind us if they had tickets. They said no. Instead of being turned away, they were told it was £10 entry.

At that point we were understandably confused, took a hot minute... then went back. I asked people in the queue whether they had tickets and every person I asked said no.

When we asked why all of these people without tickets were being allowed in when we'd just been refused, the explanation changed. We were told that the door was “curated” and that our exclusion was also a “safety” issue.

I'm 5'2", am Femme-presenting AFAB and had done absolutely nothing aggressive, threatening or inappropriate when we first approached the door... We actually accepted the reason and walked away. So being told that our presence somehow presented a “safety” issue was honestly absurd and BS. After questioning why we'd been treated differently and challenged the inconsistency with both her and the security person, I was then told that my reaction was essentially evidence of why I shouldn't be let in? That feels incredibly circular... I was perfectly civil when we first approached, and my frustration came only after watching the stated reason for refusing us immediately contradicted.

If you operate a curated door, be transparent about that. Don't tell people you're sold out or ask about tickets then immediately admit other people without tickets, and then only when challenged introduce “curation” and “safety” as the explanation.

What makes this particularly upsetting is that my friend and I are queer women. We're both bisexual, we're both femme-presenting, and we came specifically wanting to spend our night in a queer space. We can't know what assumption was made about us from looking at us, but we were clearly judged as not fitting whatever was being “curated” at the door.

Queer women do not owe anyone a particular aesthetic to prove that we're queer enough to belong in queer spaces. Femme bisexual women already deal with having our sexuality assumed or erased because of how we look.

I completely support queer venues protecting their customers and having genuine safety policies... We have read the reviews... But if you're going to exclude someone specifically on “safety” grounds, there should be something more meaningful behind that assessment than an unexplained judgement made within seconds of seeing them... Ngl was a joke to hear.

This didn't feel like a safe or inclusive space for lesbian, gay and bisexual people who don't visibly conform to a queer aesthetic...

one_star_reviews.text:
Avoid — extremely poor communication and handling of my blood samples.

I had an extremely disappointing experience with this clinic. Their communication is terrible and has resulted in misunderstandings several times, but this latest incident was by far the worst.

On Saturday morning, I had extensive blood tests done, costing me over £2,000. A significant amount of blood was taken.

On Monday, a member of staff apparently tried to contact me by SMS to confirm my name. I don’t normally check SMS, so I didn’t see the messages. Despite receiving no response, nobody thought to contact me by email or through another method. The messages themselves also provided very little context.

By Wednesday, I responded because her texts made it sound as though Wednesday was the deadline for providing the information. I then discovered that the samples were already no longer viable and had been discarded. When I called, staff initially couldn’t even identify who had been trying to contact me.

After all of this, I was casually asked to return and have the blood tests done again. I found the attitude toward the situation astonishing. This wasn’t a saliva sample — a substantial amount of blood had been taken, and I have no intention of repeating such extensive blood tests anytime soon simply because of what appears to have been a preventable communication failure.

Given the cost, inconvenience, and physical burden involved, I expected considerably more care and professionalism. I will be looking into my options regarding what happened.

I’m leaving this review to warn others about my experience. There are plenty of other clinics available, and after this incident I would personally choose somewhere that takes communication and the handling of time-sensitive samples more seriously.

I bought my Land Rover Discovery Sport from Cars 4 You Kidderminster in late 2024 for £17,500, around £23,000 in total with finance. It had roughly 80,000 miles on it.

Within one week, it went back to them for around 10 days for a timing-chain replacement. To be fair, they were helpful with this initially.

Unfortunately, that was only the beginning. After getting it back, I had a faulty battery, the stop-start wasn’t working, knocking suspension, an oil leak and a coolant leak. I contacted them and was told they would look at it if I got it back to them, despite the car being unsafe to drive. I offered to have it repaired locally and send them the bill, but we couldn’t reach an agreement.

The car has since been inspected by multiple independent garages, including the garage I’ve chosen to carry out the repairs, and the problems are considerably worse than I originally realised.

I’ve now been told the timing chain needs replacing AGAIN. I’ve also been told the oil leak relates to a seal not being replaced during previous timing-chain work, while the coolant leak was caused by a split pipe which my mechanic said appeared to have been damaged by a tool.

I’ve also discovered the car had been remapped and emissions systems deleted/disabled, including AdBlue/EGR-related modifications, none of which were disclosed when I bought it. When I raised this, they denied knowledge of it, despite me being told when purchasing that the vehicle had previously remained within the seller’s family.

I’ve also had concerns raised regarding the vehicle’s MOT history, and reading other negative reviews, I don’t appear to be the only customer to have experienced serious mechanical/MOT-related issues.

I’m now approximately £5,000–£6,000 into repairs and problems, on top of buying a £17,500 car.

To be fair, they were never rude to me and were generally polite. But being polite doesn’t change the experience I’ve had or the amount this car has cost me.

Based entirely on my own experience, I would not buy another vehicle from Cars 4 You and couldn’t recommend them. It’s been an extremely expensive lesson.
